questions.q:
Will there be more 'Explosions/Remote violence' in Latvia for the 30 days before {resolution_date} compared to the 30-day average of 'Explosions/Remote violence' over the 360 days preceding {forecast_due_date}?

e.g. If the forecast due date is 2024-01-01 and we have the following data:
Date,'Explosions/Remote violence'
2023-11-11,1
2023-10-10,2
to calculate the 30-day average of 'Explosions/Remote violence' over the preceding 360 days, we’d have: (1+2)/12=0.25.

In this example, for the question to resolve positively, 1 or more 'Explosions/Remote violence' would need to occur in the 30 days leading up to the resolution. | horizon 2026-11-01
questions.resolution_note: Resolves to the value calculated from the ACLED dataset once the data is published.

base_rate_used.reference_class: P(30-day event count exceeds its 360-day 30-day mean) for right-skewed conflict count data

evidence: Dataset family 'acled', horizon 2026-11-01: Poisson survival at freeze mean 0.16666666666666666, damped for overdispersion.
questions.strongest_opposing_case: Strongest case against: the family rule ignores series-specific news and regime changes; any structural break since the freeze date (war shocks, policy moves, product relists) would move the true probability well away from this base rate.
questions.reasoning_summary: Family base-rate strategy for acled at horizon 2026-11-01: Poisson survival at freeze mean 0.16666666666666666, damped for overdispersion. These statistical fills are the protocol's base-rate-first rule applied programmatically from the question's own freeze value; final p=0.15.
